findings: Basic two-person English dialogue is solved, even by the cheapest model. All 12 models that ran said both lines word for word, gave him a male voice and her a female voice, moved the right mouth on each line, and ended with her lowering the phone.

Veo 3.1 Lite cost $0.60 per 8-second clip, between a half and a sixth of the other models' price, and passed every check. It's the candidate for trial and error. Wan 3.0 ($1.14) and Kling 3.0 ($1.51) are the next cheapest that passed everything.
The models that cost 2–6× more (Seedance 2.0 / 2.5 / Fast, Veo 3.1 Fast) did not do anything visibly better in this scene. Whether they act better or sound more natural is for the ear to judge.

Leonardo charges more than the makers' list prices: about ×1.5 for Veo Lite and ×2–3 for most others (see Price reference). Buying Veo directly from Google with our own Gemini key would cost the list price.
A failed clip is still charged. Full Veo 3.1 (the quality benchmark) failed without giving a reason and cost $4.78, while Veo Lite and Fast accepted the same frame.

Gemini Omni Flash is out for this film. It can't take a start frame, so the room and the woman's face change during the clip (new paintings, a different face by the end). The film needs the same four people in every shot.
What the machine checks can't judge: the acting, how natural the voices sound, and small lip errors. Please watch Scene 1 with sound and pick your favourites. That's the real decision.
Next: Scene 2 (the café) is harder: a prop, longer lines and a quiet emotion. I suggest running it on the shortlist only: Veo 3.1 Lite, Veo 3.1 Fast, Kling 3.0 and Wan 3.0, for about $5.

grok-imagine-1.5.summary: Good; she lowers the phone and turns to him.
